example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, credit memo CM-0418 for Harbor Retail and every credit in September 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.CreditMemos_2026-09.xlsx: the skill's own file name for the September workpaper, made on the user's yes

messages.text: Harbor Retail needs a credit for a pricing error on invoice 1042. Can you handle it?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the documents?
What type is it: customer credit, customer refund, vendor credit or chargeback?
Which original invoice? I need its number, date and amount.
What is the reason? I never guess it.
Did the original carry tax? If so, in which jurisdiction?
Which period's credits do you want me to check?
Who approves a credit that is more than its original invoice?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. A customer credit, CM-0418, $1,200 before tax, against invoice 1042. The reason is a pricing error. Tax as on the invoice. Check all of September. Our finance director approves over-credits.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I process **credit memo CM-0418** for **Northbrook Trading**: a **customer credit** of **$1,200** against **invoice 1042**, reason **pricing error**. Tax follows the invoice. I also check every credit in **September** and list unapplied credits in both directions. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
messages.summary: 10 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Invoice 1042 was **$17,200** with 7.5% tax. So the credit carries tax too, on a line of its own. The credit is **$1,290**:

card.title: CM-0418, Harbor Retail
rows: Invoice 1042 with tax, open before the credit

messages.after: Applying a credit needs no second journal entry. The draft entry is debit Sales Returns & Allowances $1,200 and Sales Tax Payable $90. It credits Accounts Receivable $1,290.

messages.text: Then I checked every September credit. Each one must have an original, stay within it, sit in an open period, match its currency and carry the right tax. Three fail:

messages.after: Your finance director must approve the **$215**. Until then, it stays on account.

messages.text: Acme's credit CM-0412 reversed $860 with no tax line. Invoice 1019 carried $60 of tax on $800. So you still report **$60** of sales tax on a sale that you cancelled. Pinnacle's $250 credit has no original invoice. I give it no entry until you tell me its business reason.
Your unapplied credits come next, vendor credits first:

messages.after: Vendor credits total **$2,750**. Customer credits total **$2,377.50**. Delta's $400 credit went to Other Income, but bill B-5530 went to Packaging Supplies.

messages.text: I propose three draft entries. Each one points to its evidence:

messages.after: E3 and E4 correct entries already in your books. I never edit or delete the originals. A person posts these drafts. I do not post entries or send refunds.

messages.text: Your workpaper has six sheets. They are the register, the posting inputs, the application tracking, the unapplied credits, the validation exceptions and the coverage.
messages.after: Do you want the sheets as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. Here is **CreditMemos_2026-09.xlsx**. I saved your account map, the reason treatments and your approver. I never save a customer's name with an amount, or the open credit balance.
